## Purpose and entry points
Duckling is a Haskell library and optional HTTP service for extracting structured entities from natural-language text: times, numerals, quantities, money, contacts, URLs, and related dimensions. The public API and orchestration boundary are `Duckling/Api.hs`, `Duckling/Core.hs`, and `Duckling/Engine.hs`. The runnable example server is `exe/ExampleMain.hs`; integration, custom-dimension, debug, and expensive-run executables are under `exe/`.

## Request-to-entity pipeline
A caller supplies text, locale, enabled dimensions, and time context. API code converts this into a parse request, obtains locale-specific rules, invokes the rule engine, resolves semantic values, ranks overlapping candidates, and serializes entities. Core document/token/entity representations are centralized in `Duckling/Types.hs`, `Duckling/Types/Document.hs`, and `Duckling/Types/Stash.hs`. Regex matching is isolated behind `Duckling/Engine/Regex.hs` and `Duckling/Regex/Types.hs`, requiring PCRE headers at build time.

## Rule engine and semantic composition
The engine applies named rules whose patterns match text or previously produced tokens; productions compose tokens into higher-level values. Rule abstractions and language aggregators live in `Duckling/Rules.hs`, `Duckling/Rules/Common.hs`, and locale aggregators such as `Duckling/Rules/EN.hs`. Resolution of intermediate token values to final entities is a distinct stage in `Duckling/Resolve.hs`. This separates reusable parsing mechanics from language/domain grammar.

## Dimensions and value models
Each dimension owns typed semantic values, generic rules, and language-specific grammars. Representative roots are `Duckling/Time/Types.hs`, `Duckling/Numeral/Types.hs`, and `Duckling/AmountOfMoney/Types.hs`; analogous families cover duration, ordinal, quantity, distance, volume, temperature, email, URL, phone, and credit-card number. Rules commonly depend on numeral extraction, then produce normalized units, currencies, or temporal values. Time is especially substantial, including computed temporal logic and timezone parsing in `Duckling/Time/Computed.hs` and `Duckling/Time/TimeZone/Parse.hs`.

## Locale and capability selection
Locale/region modeling determines which language and regional variants participate in a request: `Duckling/Locale.hs`, `Duckling/Region.hs`, and `Duckling/Dimensions/Types.hs`. Per-language dimension registries, e.g. `Duckling/Dimensions/EN.hs` and `Duckling/Dimensions/ZH.hs`, expose supported dimensions. Locale-specific extensions encode material regional differences, such as `Duckling/Time/EN/US/Rules.hs` and `Duckling/AmountOfMoney/EN/GB/Rules.hs`, without changing the common engine.

## Candidate ranking
The parser can produce competing or overlapping extractions. Ranking extracts feature representations and selects preferred entities using generated locale classifiers: `Duckling/Ranking/Extraction.hs`, `Duckling/Ranking/Rank.hs`, and `Duckling/Ranking/Classifiers.hs`. Generated classifier modules are locale-specific, for example `Duckling/Ranking/Classifiers/EN_US.hs`; regeneration/training entry points are `exe/RegenMain.hs`, `exe/Duckling/Ranking/Generate.hs`, and `exe/Duckling/Ranking/Train.hs`.

## Delivery and infrastructure
The project is built as a Cabal/Stack Haskell package (`duckling.cabal`, `stack.yaml`) and containerized through `Dockerfile`. GitHub Actions CI is defined in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No persistent datastore or required external runtime service is evident; the optional HTTP server is a local adapter over the library, while wit.ai is mentioned only as an alternative hosted integration.
